en: Job 9

p.src: 1  Then Job answered,

en: Then Job answered,
u.src: 1  Then Job answered,

p.src: 2  “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

en: “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?
u.src: 2  “Truly I know that it is so, but how can man be just with God?

p.src: 3  If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

en: If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.
u.src: 3  If he is pleased to contend with him, he can’t answer him one time in a thousand.

p.src: 4  God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?

en: God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?
u.src: 4  God is wise in heart, and mighty in strength. Who has hardened himself against him and prospered?

p.src: 5  He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

en: He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.
u.src: 5  He removes the mountains, and they don’t know it, when he overturns them in his anger.

p.src: 6  He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

en: He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
u.src: 6  He shakes the earth out of its place. Its pillars tremble.

p.src: 7  He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.

en: He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.
u.src: 7  He commands the sun and it doesn’t rise, and seals up the stars.

p.src: 8  He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

en: He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.
u.src: 8  He alone stretches out the heavens, and treads on the waves of the sea.

p.src: 9  He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

en: He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.
u.src: 9  He makes the Bear, Orion, and the Pleiades, and the rooms of the south.

p.src: 10  He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

en: He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.
u.src: 10  He does great things past finding out; yes, marvelous things without number.

p.src: 11  Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

en: Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.
u.src: 11  Behold, he goes by me, and I don’t see him. He passes on also, but I don’t perceive him.

p.src: 12  Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

en: Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’
u.src: 12  Behold, he snatches away. Who can hinder him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?’

p.src: 13  “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

en: “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.
u.src: 13  “God will not withdraw his anger. The helpers of Rahab stoop under him.

p.src: 14  How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?

en: How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?
u.src: 14  How much less will I answer him, and choose my words to argue with him?

p.src: 15  Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

en: Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.
u.src: 15  Though I were righteous, yet I wouldn’t answer him. I would make supplication to my judge.

p.src: 16  If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

en: If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.
u.src: 16  If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn’t believe that he listened to my voice.

p.src: 17  For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

en: For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
u.src: 17  For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.

p.src: 18  He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

en: He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
u.src: 18  He will not allow me to catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.

p.src: 19  If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

en: If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’
u.src: 19  If it is a matter of strength, behold, he is mighty! If of justice, ‘Who,’ says he, ‘will summon me?’

p.src: 20  Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.

en: Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.
u.src: 20  Though I am righteous, my own mouth will condemn me. Though I am blameless, it will prove me perverse.

p.src: 21  I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.

en: I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.
u.src: 21  I am blameless. I don’t respect myself. I despise my life.

p.src: 22  “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

en: “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.
u.src: 22  “It is all the same. Therefore I say he destroys the blameless and the wicked.

p.src: 23  If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

en: If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.
u.src: 23  If the scourge kills suddenly, he will mock at the trial of the innocent.

p.src: 24  The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

en: The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?
u.src: 24  The earth is given into the hand of the wicked. He covers the faces of its judges. If not he, then who is it?

p.src: 25  “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.

en: “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.
u.src: 25  “Now my days are swifter than a runner. They flee away. They see no good.

p.src: 26  They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

en: They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
u.src: 26  They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.

p.src: 27  If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’

en: If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’
u.src: 27  If I say, ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad face, and cheer up,’

p.src: 28  I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.

en: I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.
u.src: 28  I am afraid of all my sorrows. I know that you will not hold me innocent.

p.src: 29  I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

en: I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?
u.src: 29  I will be condemned. Why then do I labor in vain?

p.src: 30  If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

en: If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,
u.src: 30  If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my hands with lye,

p.src: 31  yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.

en: yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.
u.src: 31  yet you will plunge me in the ditch. My own clothes will abhor me.

p.src: 32  For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

en: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.
u.src: 32  For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, that we should come together in judgment.

p.src: 33  There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

en: There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.
u.src: 33  There is no umpire between us, that might lay his hand on us both.

p.src: 34  Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

en: Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;
u.src: 34  Let him take his rod away from me. Let his terror not make me afraid;

p.src: 35  then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.

en: then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
u.src: 35  then I would speak, and not fear him, for I am not so in myself.
